chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Sayyari, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Abdillah al-Farisi, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man said to him, 'I drank milk and it harmed me.' He said, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'No, by Allah, milk does not harm at all, but you ate it with something else, so that which you ate harmed you, and you thought that harm was from the milk.'

key_terms.الْفَارِسِيِّ: The Persian (a descriptor for the narrator Ubayd Allah)

ai.seo_question: Why did the man feel harmed after drinking milk according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that milk is inherently pure and harmless, illustrating the Shia principle of *asl al-sahha* (presumption of original purity) in food consumption. He attributes the narrator's discomfort to the *muqarrin* (accompanying food) rather than the milk itself, correcting the common error of misattributing causality to the primary substance. This hadith serves as a foundational text in *fiqh al-akl* (jurisprudence of eating), distinguishing between intrinsic impurity and external contamination.
